org.name: Tameside and Glossop Clinical Commissioning Group

theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: John Derwent
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The Inquest heard that the target time for an appointment for CBT should be 6 weeks. At the time Mr Derwent was referred, the waiting time was 12 months. There was a waiting list review in October 2017 when it was established that 500 people were on the waiting list for CBT. The waiting list time at the date of the Inquest remained 12 months. The Inquest heard that there was insufficient capacity for the number of people referred for CBT which is why the waiting list had become so significant.

reports.title: Heather Carey
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The CCG is formally monitoring the impact of this investment through regular Safer Staffing Reports presented to the Pennine Care Quality Group. Reports from staff on the Tameside wards and the latest CQC report indicate that this is having a positive impact.
promises.summary: Monitoring inpatient staffing impact via Safer Staffing Reports to ensure safety improvements

promises.quote: The reviewing team are using this information alongside an exploration of alternative models of care to develop a new model of psychological therapy for people with complex mental health needs in Tameside and Glossop. This review will conclude by the 31 of July 2019.
promises.summary: Conduct Psychological Therapies Review to improve access and quality of therapy services

promises.quote: An additional £271,000 agreed in 2018/19 will be increased by an additional £673,000 per annum by 2021 to meet a range of pressures.
promises.summary: Increase funding for psychological therapy services to reduce waiting times

promises.quote: the CCG is advised that due to actions taken internally the current waiting times for the service have improved, with a current waiting time for Cognitive Analytical Therapy of 13 weeks.
promises.summary: Report improved waiting times for Cognitive Analytical Therapy service

promises.quote: have asked the Secondary Care Psychological Therapy Service to ensure that that when people are advised about the waiting times that they are supported to work with their care coordinator for stabilisation, containment and pre therapy work in preparation for therapy to ensure that they do not suffer the distress and despair that Ms [name redacted] family state that Ms Carey experienced and evidenced by her tragic death
promises.summary: Provide pre-therapy support to reduce patient distress during waiting periods

concerns.quote: The inquest identified a number of issues which likely contributed to Heather's decision to end her life. One of those issues related to the long wait following discharge before psychotherapy would begin.
concerns.hazard: long wait for psychotherapy after discharge

concerns.quote: A target waiting list of 18 weeks is far too long but | was told that this was a funding issue.

Unless adequate and sufficient measures are taken to significantly reduce waiting times for acute mental ill-health, comparable to physical life threatening illnesses, NOT simply a redistribution of existing resources, more patients with mental health issues will end their lives while on a waiting list for treatment.
concerns.hazard: inadequate waiting time reduction for mental health crises

links.explanation: Both reports highlight excessively long waiting times for cognitive behavioural therapy/psychotherapy as a serious safety concern. The earlier report attributes the delay to insufficient service capacity, while the later report cites funding limitations as the cause.
links.earlier_quote: The Inquest heard that the target time for an appointment for CBT should be 6 weeks. At the time Mr Derwent was referred, the waiting time was 12 months.
links.later_quote: A target waiting list of 18 weeks is far too long but | was told that this was a funding issue.

followups.summary: The promised review was expected to conclude by 31 July 2019, but no source confirms it was completed or published by that date.
